question: Can a public DLSU fish-collection catalog, the cited Phase II environmental-monitoring completion report, or the related DLSU repository records resolve the Pasig specimen trail or the Phase II date-by-station fish matrix?

publicFishCollectionCatalog.pageAsReported: The portal says it searches 8 Philippine museums/collections and 26 international museums. Its Philippine list names UPV, MSU-IIT, USC, Silliman University, UP-MSI, the National Museum, Xavier University, and SPCP; DLSU is not among them.
publicFishCollectionCatalog.result: This public aggregator does not expose a searchable DLSU ZC-F collection in its displayed Philippine collection list, so it cannot provide the Pasig voucher crosswalk sought here.
publicFishCollectionCatalog.scopeLimit: The page reports 54,921 records and 3,350 species and was last edited 2014-02-14. DLSU's absence from this portal is not evidence that DLSU has no collection, no internal catalog, or no unindexed records. No complete DLSU-catalog query was possible through this interface.

primary2006Article.reviewedSections: Methods/site descriptions, specimen references and captions, Table 3 site codes and site-level measurement columns, and acknowledgements.
findings: The paper defines DLSU ZC-F as the De La Salle University Zoological Collection–Fishes catalog abbreviation and reports Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus at its Pasig River, City of Manila site; Pasig fish were hand-caught.
The paper's named specimen numbers in Figures 2–4 are explicitly associated with Laguna de Bay specimens, not the Pasig site.

Table 3 codes Pasig River as site 4 and provides mean morphometric measurements by study site, but it does not provide site-specific specimen counts or catalog numbers. The reported totals of 96 P. disjunctivus and 97 P. pardalis are across the study's sites, not Pasig counts.
No Pasig-specific collection date, voucher ID, count, or coordinate was found in the reviewed article.

dlsuRepository.thesisResult: The accessible 2005 thesis metadata and abstract report the same five-site study and Pasig-only P. disjunctivus result as the 2006 article. The repository's linked full-text endpoint returned HTTP 403 in the browser retrieval; no access control was bypassed, and no thesis-specific specimen table was reviewed.
dlsuRepository.proceedingResult: The DLSU Research Congress 2014 record identifies an eight-site Luzon Pterygoplichthys survey and says invasion stages ranged from II to V. Its repository entry has no uploaded file, and the abstract does not identify the eight waterbody/site names or join them to dated specimen records.
dlsuRepository.lineageLimit: The 2005 thesis abstract duplicates the 2006 article-level summary and is not an independent survey confirmation. The 2014 abstract is a new regional research lead, not a site-resolved occurrence table.

searches: Exact report title with PMRCIP and Phase II
site:dpwh.gov.ph with the exact Phase II environmental-monitoring completion-report title
site:eia.emb.gov.ph with the exact report title and Pasig
site:jica.go.jp and site:openjicareport.jica.go.jp with the report title and PMRCIP Phase II
phaseIIReportSearch.result: Search results continued to lead to the official 2018 Phase IV EIS, which cites the 2013 Phase II completion report and reproduces summary tables, but no separate accessible copy of the cited report or fish voucher ledger was located.
phaseIIReportSearch.limit: A bounded public web search does not establish that the report is unavailable from project archives or through other access routes. The EIS's richness totals and unlinked narrative taxon list remain secondary summaries, not a station-by-date specimen matrix.

evidenceDecision.reason: The catalog portal does not include DLSU in its displayed Philippine collection list; the DLSU thesis is available only as metadata/abstract in this retrieval, and the 2014 proceedings entry has no attached full text. The primary 2006 paper's named voucher figures are from Laguna de Bay, while its Pasig-specific voucher/date/count are not printed. The cited PMRCIP report remains unlocated in bounded public searches.

nonClaims: DLSU's absence from FishBase's displayed Philippine collection list does not establish absence of a DLSU catalog or physical specimens.
A repository HTTP 403 is an access limitation, not evidence about the contents of the inaccessible thesis or a reason to bypass access controls.
The eight-site count in the 2014 abstract does not identify individual waterbodies or establish current Pterygoplichthys presence at them.
The zero new records and inaccessible materials in this review do not establish fish absence from Pasig River or any other Luzon waterbody.
The 2013 Phase II completion report remains a retrieval lead; no date, station, taxon, method, voucher, or count crosswalk was inferred from the 2018 EIS summary.
nextActions: Continue NCR source discovery across freshwater, brackish, marine, and wetland lanes; keep the shared Pasig/Marikina system distinct from capture-site assignments.
Prioritize additional public, reusable, site-resolved sources rather than treating the unavailable Phase II report or the DLSU abstract-only records as data feeds.

If the DLSU ZC-F catalog or a public extract becomes available through an authorized route, match records to the complete Pasig locality and collection event before changing the historical evidence decision.
Keep this review research-only; no contact, login, download workaround, or external request was made.
